searchDocs.title: Auto Accept Campaign
searchDocs.content: Auto Accept Campaign An Auto Accept campaign is an automatic campaign that automatically accepts connection invites. Each profile has a single Auto-Accept campaign by default.

searchDocs.title: How do you define steps​
searchDocs.content: Steps are defined from the Steps Tab. Most campaigns will come come with default steps:

searchDocs.title: The structure of a Step​
searchDocs.content: Most steps will contain either all or some of the following options

searchDocs.title: 1. Template strings​
searchDocs.content: Instead of sending general messages, Sonity allows you to send personalized messages through template string for example if click firstname literal  Hi {firstname}, how are you?  It will substitute firstname for every contact's name for example  Hi John, how are you? Hi Grace, how are you? Hi Mark, how are you?

searchDocs.title: 2. Main Message​
searchDocs.content: Main message is the main message that gets send if no issues occur.

searchDocs.title: 3. Like Post before interacton​
searchDocs.content: This will like a contact's post before sending the message. Interacting with a contact's content before sending an unsolicitated message or a connection request has been proven to increase success

searchDocs.title: 4. Fallback Message​
searchDocs.content: When parsing issues occur, the fallback message gets sent. This ensures that the contact recieves the message even when an issue occur.

searchDocs.title: 5. Delay​
searchDocs.content: A step is usually executed immediately (As long as the driver is in its execution window). However you may prefer sending the message after a certain delay. For example if a contact accepts your message you wouldn't want to execute a welcome message immediately and it will look fishy.

searchDocs.title: Types if steps​
searchDocs.content: There are many types of steps. However before diving into the steps please take a note of this:  - Steps are unique in the way they are executed, so you cant send a Welcome Message using a Connection Message step and vise versa. So use a step for its intended purpose.- Connection Message and Welcome Message steps should be run once per contact in a campaign

searchDocs.title: 1. Connection Message Step​
searchDocs.content: This step is used to send an Invite message to a contact. If this step succeeds you will have a new connection. Its mostly used in a Connection Campaign.

searchDocs.title: 2. Welcome Message​
searchDocs.content: This step is used to send a Welcome message after a successful connection.

searchDocs.title: 3. Message Step​
searchDocs.content: This is used to a message to to a contact. Unlike a Welcome or Connection message, you can have more of these:

searchDocs.title: 4. Endorsement Step​
searchDocs.content: This step is used to endorse a random skill for every contact in that campaign. You can use use this either before or after other steps

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: Every campaign moves through the following stages:  Plan -> Build -> Launch -> Engagement -> Optimization -> Completion -> Repeat / Scale  This is not a one-time process. It is a loop. Each campaign teaches you something you can apply to the next.

searchDocs.title: 1. Plan​
searchDocs.content: This is where your campaign begins.  Define:  Your target audience (for example founders, recruiters, developers)Your goal (lead generation, hiring, networking)Your messaging angle  A strong plan sets the foundation for everything that follows.

searchDocs.title: 2. Build​
searchDocs.content: Create your campaign inside Sonity.  This includes:  Importing contacts (search, CSV, profile URLs)Defining your sequence: Connection requestMessageFollow-ups Setting delays and timing between actions  This step turns your idea into an automated workflow.

searchDocs.title: 3. Launch​
searchDocs.content: Activate your campaign.  Once launched:  Connection requests are sent automaticallyMessages follow based on your defined sequenceActivity runs within safe daily limits  At this stage, your campaign is live and running.

searchDocs.title: 4. Engagement​
searchDocs.content: This is where real interactions happen.  Your contacts may:  Accept your connection requestReply to your messagesIgnore the outreach  You may need to:  Respond to repliesQualify leadsMove conversations forward  This stage directly impacts your results.

searchDocs.title: 5. Optimization​
searchDocs.content: Review and improve your campaign performance.  Monitor:  Acceptance rateReply rateDrop-off points in your sequence  Adjust:  Messaging contentTarget audienceTiming between steps  Optimization is what turns an average campaign into a high-performing one.

searchDocs.title: 6. Completion​
searchDocs.content: A campaign reaches completion when:  All contacts have been processedYou manually stop or pause itYour goal has been achieved  At this point, you can evaluate results and prepare for the next iteration.

searchDocs.title: 7. Repeat / Scale​
searchDocs.content: Use what you have learned to improve and expand.  You can:  Duplicate and refine successful campaignsTarget new audiencesRun multiple campaigns simultaneously  Scaling allows you to grow outreach while maintaining performance.

searchDocs.title: Key Takeaway​
searchDocs.content: Campaigns are not static. They are iterative systems.  The most successful users continuously:  Learn from resultsImprove their approachRun better campaigns over time

searchDocs.title: 1. Connector Campaigns​
searchDocs.content: Connector Campaigns are designed to send connection requests to targeted prospects, helping you grow your professional network and start building relationships with potential leads.

searchDocs.title: 2. Messenger Campaigns​
searchDocs.content: Messenger Campaigns allow you to send direct messages to your connections, making it easier to nurture relationships, follow up with prospects, and share relevant information in a personal way.

searchDocs.title: 3. InMail Campaigns​
searchDocs.content: InMail Campaigns are used to reach people outside of your direct network through LinkedIn InMail, enabling you to contact high-value prospects even if you are not yet connected.

searchDocs.title: 4. Schedule Post Campaign​
searchDocs.content: Schedule Post Campaigns help you plan and publish content automatically at selected times, ensuring consistent posting and improving audience engagement without requiring manual updates.

searchDocs.title: 5. Auto Accept Campaign​
searchDocs.content: Auto Accept Campaigns automatically accept incoming connection requests, helping you expand your network faster and maintain momentum in your outreach efforts.

searchDocs.title: 6. Flow Campaign​
searchDocs.content: Flow Campaigns help you structure outreach in a more natural way by spacing interactions and combining actions such as connection requests, messages, and other engagement steps.

searchDocs.title: What's Sonity?​
searchDocs.content: Sonity is a cutting-edge LinkedIn automation tool designed to revolutionize the way professionals connect and engage on the platform. With a sleek interface and powerful features, Sonity empowers users to optimize their LinkedIn presence effortlessly.

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: Advanced search filters: Precisely target your ideal audience based on various criteria.Automated connection requests: Efficiently expand your network with personalized outreach.Intelligent messaging: Craft engaging messages tailored to different recipient segments.Campaign management: Create and execute targeted campaigns for maximum impact.In-depth analytics: Track campaign performance and optimize strategies.Lead generation: Identify and nurture potential customers.  Sonity's AI-driven algorithms ensure optimal results by automating repetitive tasks and providing valuable insights. By harnessing the power of Sonity, professionals can significantly enhance their LinkedIn success and achieve their business goals.

searchDocs.title: How does Sonity work​
searchDocs.content: You add your profileYou create a campaign and define campaign stepsSonity does the rest  tip Sonity also support steps generation using AI

searchDocs.title: FAQ​
searchDocs.content: Sonity has many components, but here are just a few:  What is a Campaign? A collection of steps designed to achieve a specific goal. What are contacts? A list of individuals or companies targeted by a campaign.Contacts are added to a campaign via running a search & collect, CSV import or reusing exisiting contacts What are Steps? Individual actions within a campaign (e.g., send connection request, send message). What is a Profile? Represents the user account performing actions within the campaign. This profile maps to a a social media account. What are webhooks? A webhook is a URL that recieves real time events and notifications.In Sonity they are used for receiving realtime updates on what is taking place in the app

searchDocs.title: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
Why Sonity built an MCP server​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Before MCP, getting an AI to act on your Sonity data meant either hand-pasting information into a chat window or writing bespoke integrations per client. With the Sonity MCP server:  No copy-paste. The AI reads your campaigns, leads, and profiles directly.One integration, many clients. Any MCP-compatible app can connect with the same URL + token.Scoped, revocable access. You authorize the server with a short-lived, scoped token from inside Sonity — nothing is ever permanently handed out.

searchDocs.title: What you need​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: A Sonity account with at least one profile.A supported MCP client (see table below).A Sonity authorization token, generated from the in-app MCP dialog. See Authentication.

searchDocs.title: How it fits together​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Your AI client sends a JSON-RPC request to the MCP server with your Bearer token.The MCP server verifies the token, translates the request into a Sonity GraphQL query (or a driver call for direct_search_and_collect), and signs it as HS256 before forwarding it.The GraphQL API / driver performs the action against your Sonity data and returns the result.The MCP server hands the result back to the AI client as plain text.

searchDocs.title: Supported clients​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Any client that implements the MCP spec works. The ones we test against:  Client	Transport	NotesClaude Desktop	HTTP	Native MCP support. Cursor	HTTP	Configured via ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Zed	HTTP	Configured via Zed settings. Cline	HTTP	Configured via cline_mcp_settings.json. Custom scripts	HTTP or stdio	Use the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk or raw JSON-RPC. See Connecting.

searchDocs.title: What the server can and cannot do​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Can  List your Sonity profiles and resolve a sonity_profile_id.List, create, and update campaign definitions.Add or update campaign steps (your outreach sequence).Run search-and-collect jobs (with or without an existing campaign).Attach collected leads to a campaign.Fetch campaign metrics (TCP summary + meeting metrics).Send one-off messages to a specific lead.  Cannot  Send LinkedIn messages outside of a campaign step or the messaging_send tool.*Bypass LinkedIn's daily limits. All LinkedIn-side actions still go through Sonity's normal rate-limited execution pipeline.Modify your Sonity account billing, users, or passwords. Those are admin-only and not exposed via MCP.  tip We are working towards supporting the ability to send message over MCP, even outside of a campaigns  tip The full tool reference, including required arguments and which scopes each needs, is in MCP tools.

searchDocs.title: Where to next​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Introduction to the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Authentication — how to get a token and how the server verifies it.Connecting a client — copy-paste config for Claude, Cursor, Zed, Cline, and raw cURL.MCP tools — every tool the server exposes, with arguments.Troubleshooting — common errors and how to fix them.

searchDocs.title: Common errors and what they mean
"Campaign is paused"​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Common errors and what they mean
searchDocs.content: This usually means one of the following:  Daily limits were reached.A connected profile is unavailable.A required step is not configured correctly.  Check limits first, then profile status, then step configuration.

searchDocs.title: "Requests are not sending"​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Common errors and what they mean
searchDocs.content: Typical causes:  Profile execution window is closed.The campaign has no eligible contacts in the current step.LinkedIn limits were reached for the day.  Review profile settings and campaign step progress.

searchDocs.title: "Unable to parse personalization fields"​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Common errors and what they mean
searchDocs.content: A template variable is missing in contact data. For example, using {firstname} when a contact has no first name value.  Fix by:  Completing missing contact fields.Adding fallback messages in your steps.Testing templates before launch.

searchDocs.title: "Import failed for CSV"​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Common errors and what they mean
searchDocs.content: Common reasons:  Unsupported file structure.Missing required columns.Invalid profile URLs.  Re-export your CSV with clean LinkedIn profile URLs and retry.

searchDocs.content: Give your campaign a name. You can also pick a seed campaign if you have one.

searchDocs.title: Step 4: Find your contacts​
searchDocs.content: Do a search on LinkedIn (or Sales Navigator), then collect and copy the search URL.

searchDocs.title: Step 5: Paste the URL and continue​
searchDocs.content: Paste the search URL into the campaign and click Next.  You can also add contacts using profile URLs or a CSV import.

searchDocs.title: Step 6: Add steps and continue​
searchDocs.content: Open the Steps tab and configure your message flow, then click Next.  Not sure where to start? See Campaign Steps.

searchDocs.title: Step 7: Create the campaign​
searchDocs.content: Review your campaign and click Create campaign.

searchDocs.title: Step 8: You are up and running​
searchDocs.content: Your campaign has been created. Monitor its progress from your campaign reports – see Monitoring Campaigns.    For deeper concepts, explore the Campaigns section.

searchDocs.title: Is it necessary to keep my browser and laptop active while Sonity is operational?
searchDocs.content: Is it necessary to keep my browser and laptop active while Sonity is operational? No, you don't need to. Sonity serves as a comprehensive autopilot for LinkedIn, operating seamlessly even when you close your browser or turn off your laptop.

searchDocs.title: Tips and Tricks for Effective Automation
Start Slow and Gradual​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Tips and Tricks for Effective Automation
searchDocs.content: Initiate with a slow and gradual automation approach to prevent triggering LinkedIn's spam filters. Mirror natural human behavior by incrementally increasing connection requests and messages.

searchDocs.title: Targeted Connection Requests​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Tips and Tricks for Effective Automation
searchDocs.content: Send connection requests to individuals who align with your professional interests or industry. Personalize connection requests with a brief, relevant message to enhance the likelihood of acceptance.  Sonity also allows you to use AI to generate more personalized messages from the 'Variants' section.

searchDocs.title: Limit Daily Activities​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Tips and Tricks for Effective Automation
searchDocs.content: Set reasonable limits on the number of connection requests, messages, and profile views per day. Mimic human behavior by spreading out your activities over time.  You can set or adjust your activity limits from the Profiles page.

searchDocs.title: Monitor and adjust​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Tips and Tricks for Effective Automation
searchDocs.content: Regularly monitor the performance of your automation tool. Adjust your settings based on the responses and engagement you receive. If certain actions are not yielding positive results, consider tweaking your approach. You can monitor your campaign from the Reports section of your campaign.  For more information check this guide:  Reports section of your campaign.

searchDocs.title: Use Proxies​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Tips and Tricks for Effective Automation
searchDocs.content: Consider using proxies to avoid detection. Proxies can help distribute activity across different IP addresses, reducing the risk of being flagged. In Sonity, proxies are set and managed on a profile basis. You can change proxies from the Profile settings.    Under your profile settings, click on the Proxy dropdown to reveal the new proxy button. Click this to create a new proxy.    Give your proxy a name and specify the host (as an IP e.g. 127.0.0.1) and the port Sonity can use to connect to it. If your proxy is password protected, check the “Password protected” option and it will reveal another section you can use to enter the authentication details to connect to it.    After this, you can simply click the “Add Proxy” button to confirm your proxy connection.

searchDocs.title: Generating Posts
searchDocs.content: Generating Posts To generate posts using AI, follow these steps: On the campaign page go to the Steps Tab Under a specific post, upload a photo, add some short text on what you want to generate then click Generate Button tip Do not forget to add mention the target topic. This will help the AI generate a more relevant post. Wait for the AI to generate the post Click the Preview button to see how the post will look in Linked In

searchDocs.title: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
Two ways to authenticate​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: You can sign in to the Sonity MCP server in two ways. Pick the one that matches how you're connecting.  Sign in with Sonity (recommended) — the easy way. You click a button in Sonity, approve what the AI client is allowed to do, and Sonity hands the client a token. Use this for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed, Cline, and the in-app MCP dialog. This is the standard "log in with..." flow you've seen on other websites.Paste a Sonity session token — for scripts or advanced setups where opening a browser isn't practical. You copy a long-lived token from your Sonity session and paste it into your client.  No matter which way you sign in, the MCP server only uses your token to talk to Sonity on your behalf. Your token is never shared with anyone else.

searchDocs.title: What happens when you click "Authorize MCP"​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Behind the scenes, Sonity uses a secure sign-in standard called OAuth. Don't worry about the details — here's roughly what happens when you click the button:  You click Authorize MCP in the Sonity dialog.If you're not signed in, Sonity asks you to sign in first.Sonity shows you a list of permissions the AI client wants (for example: read your data, write changes). You review them and click Allow.Sonity generates a short-lived access token (good for 1 hour) and a refresh token (good for 30 days). The access token is what your AI client will use to talk to Sonity.The dialog shows you the access token to copy. Paste it into your AI client's MCP settings.When the access token expires after an hour, your client uses the refresh token behind the scenes to get a new one. You usually don't need to do anything — it just keeps working for 30 days. After 30 days, you'll click Authorize MCP again to get a fresh pair.

searchDocs.title: Token lifetimes (in plain English)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Access token — the one your client uses to make requests. Lasts 1 hour. When it expires, your client should automatically swap it for a new one using the refresh token. You usually won't notice.Refresh token — lasts 30 days. Used behind the scenes to get new access tokens. After 30 days, just click Authorize MCP again in the Sonity dialog to get a new pair.  When the access token expires, your client can quietly get a new one using the refresh token. You don't need to do this yourself — your AI client handles it automatically. (Advanced users: the call is POST /oauth/token with grant_type=refresh_token.)

searchDocs.title: Scopes​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: When you click Authorize MCP, Sonity shows you a list of permissions the AI client is asking for. These are called scopes — they're a way of saying "yes, you can do this, but not that." You'll see the same descriptions on the consent screen:  Scope	What it lets the AI client domcp:read	Read your Sonity data (campaigns, leads, profiles, tasks). mcp:write	Create or update Sonity data on your behalf. profile	See your basic profile information. sonity_account_id	Know which Sonity account it's acting on.  The Sonity dialog asks for all four by default. The sonity_account_id scope is required — without it, the server can't tell which account you're using, and every request will fail.

searchDocs.title: How to get a token from the Sonity UI​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Sign in to Sonity at https://app.sonity.net.Open the sidebar and click the MCP connection entry (the Bot icon near your account menu).Click Authorize MCP. If you aren't signed in, you'll be asked to sign in first. After signing in you'll come right back here. On the MCP Authorization consent page, review the permissions and click Allow.You'll be taken back to Sonity. The dialog now shows two things: MCP endpoint URL: https://app.sonity.net/mcpAuthorization header: Authorization: Bearer <your-access-token> Copy both into your AI client's MCP settings. See Connecting a client for step-by-step help with each client.  caution The access token expires in 1 hour. If your client stops working later, come back to this dialog and click Authorize MCP again to get a fresh one. The dialog will show you the new value to copy.

searchDocs.title: How to revoke access​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: If you ever want to disconnect an AI client:  Quick local clear (in the MCP dialog, click Remove MCP authorization) — Sonity forgets the token in your browser. Useful if you just want to clean up. Note: the token itself is still valid on the server until it expires, so this is mostly cosmetic.Fully revoke it on the server — if you've lost a device or want to be safe, ask your admin to revoke the refresh token. After that, the AI client can't get new access tokens. Any access token that's already out there still works until it expires (max 1 hour).

searchDocs.title: Security notes​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Never share the token. Don't paste it into a chat, commit it to a repo, or screenshot it. Treat it like a password.The token only works for your Sonity account. A token for account A cannot access account B.Your token is never sent to anything outside Sonity. The MCP server uses it only to talk to Sonity on your behalf. You don't need to worry about the technical details — just know it's safe by design.

searchDocs.title: Where to next​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Authenticating with the Sonity MCP server
searchDocs.content: Connecting a client — paste your token into Claude, Cursor, Zed, Cline, or a script.MCP tools — what you can call once authenticated.Troubleshooting — invalid token, missing scopes, expired tokens.

searchDocs.title: Tool reference​
searchDocs.content: Tool	Purpose	Required arguments	Needs mcp:write?profiles	List your Sonity profiles; resolve a sonity_profile_id.	— (account derived from JWT)	No campaigns_list	List campaign definitions for a profile.	optional sonity_profile_id	No campaigns_create	Create a new campaign definition.	name, sonity_profile_id	Yes campaigns_update	Update a campaign (rename, pause, activate, etc.).	id	Yes add_campaign_steps	Bulk upsert message steps on an existing campaign.	campaign_definition_id, values	Yes campaign_metrics	Fetch TCP summary + meeting metrics for a campaign.	campaign_definition_id	No run_search_and_collect	Create a search-and-collect task for an existing campaign.	sonity_profile_id, campaign_definition_id, url	Yes direct_search_and_collect	Run search-and-collect directly against the driver, no campaign needed.	sonity_profile_id, keywords	Yes add_leads_to_campaign	Attach a batch of leads to a campaign.	campaign_definition_id, sonity_profile_id, values	Yes leads_search	Free-text lead search.	query	No messaging_send	Send a one-off message to a specific lead.	leadId, text	Yes  The sonity_account_id you are acting on is read from the JWT sonity_account_id claim — you never pass it as an argument.

searchDocs.title: Typical workflow​
searchDocs.content: Most non-trivial sessions follow this shape: resolve a profile, create or pick a campaign, add steps, run search-and-collect to find leads, attach them to the campaign, then watch the metrics.

searchDocs.title: profiles​
searchDocs.content: List all Sonity profiles belonging to your account. Each profile is a connected LinkedIn/CRM identity. Call this first to resolve the sonity_profile_id that most other tools require.  Arguments: none meaningful. (sonity_account_id is taken from the JWT; passing it does nothing.)

searchDocs.title: campaigns_list​
searchDocs.content: List campaign definitions for a profile. Returns id, name, type, start_date, set_active, set_inmail, and timestamps.  Arguments:  sonity_profile_id (optional) — filter to one profile. Omit to list campaigns across all your profiles.

searchDocs.title: campaigns_create​
searchDocs.content: Create a new campaign definition. Returns the created campaign including its id.  Arguments:  name (required) — campaign name.sonity_profile_id (required) — profile that owns the campaign (from profiles).type (optional) — one of Connector, SchedulePosts, Messenger, InMail. Omit if unsure.extensions (optional) — { requeue_errors?: boolean, requeue_withdrawn?: boolean }.campaign_messages (optional) — initial sequence of message steps to create with the campaign. See The {variable} fallback rule below.auto_fallback (optional) — see below.

searchDocs.title: campaigns_update​
searchDocs.content: Update fields of an existing campaign. Only pass the fields you want to change.  Arguments:  id (required) — campaign definition id (from campaigns_list).name, sonity_profile_id, start_date, set_active, set_inmail, type, extensions — any subset.  Use this to rename a campaign, activate it (set_active: true), pause it (set_active: false), enable InMail mode, or reschedule it.

searchDocs.title: add_campaign_steps​
searchDocs.content: Bulk upsert (insert or update) message steps on an existing campaign. Pass one entry per step; include id to update an existing step, or omit it to create a new one. Steps are ordered by the step field (0-based).  Arguments:  campaign_definition_id (required).values (required) — array of step objects, each with step (0-based index), type (e.g. Connection Message, Welcome Message), text, and optional delay, fallback_text, inmail_subject, like_post, skip_message, complete_time, extensions.auto_fallback (optional) — see below.

searchDocs.title: campaign_metrics​
searchDocs.content: Fetch performance metrics for a campaign: a TCP (touch/conversion) summary table plus meeting metrics (contacts, requests, connections, replies, errors).  Arguments:  campaign_definition_id (required).sonity_profile_id (optional) — scope the TCP summary.campaign_definition_names (optional) — additional name filter for the TCP summary.timeRange (optional) — [start, end] pair of ISO 8601 timestamps.

searchDocs.title: run_search_and_collect​
searchDocs.content: Create a search-and-collect task attached to an existing campaign. Use this when you already have a campaign_definition_id and a LinkedIn search URL. The driver visits profiles from that URL and attaches them to the campaign.  Arguments:  sonity_profile_id (required).campaign_definition_id (required) — the campaign to attach collected leads to.url (required) — LinkedIn search URL to collect leads from.visit_max (optional, default 150) — max profile visits.

searchDocs.title: direct_search_and_collect​
searchDocs.content: Run a search-and-collect job directly against the driver without creating a campaign first. Use this when the user has no campaign_definition_id — only keywords. Returns collected lead records you can then pass to add_leads_to_campaign.  Arguments:  sonity_profile_id (required).keywords (required) — search keywords (job title, company, skill, etc.).visit_max (optional, default 20) — max profile visits.network_distance (optional) — array of 1st, 2nd, 3rd.location (optional) — array of LinkedIn location URNs (e.g. urn:li:geo:101174742).

searchDocs.title: add_leads_to_campaign​
searchDocs.content: Attach a batch of leads to an existing campaign. Each lead is queued into the campaign; Sonity creates a contact and prospect for each and links them to the campaign. Use this after direct_search_and_collect (or run_search_and_collect) to enroll collected leads for sequenced outreach.  Arguments:  campaign_definition_id (required).sonity_profile_id (required) — applied to every lead in the batch.values (required) — array of lead objects. Only l_id (the LinkedIn public slug, e.g. victor-jayeoba-400b96253) is required per lead; optional fields include name, href, title, first_name, last_name, connection_type, current_position, location, description, thumb, thread_l_id.

searchDocs.title: leads_search​
searchDocs.content: Free-text search across your existing Sonity leads by name, company, title, etc. Returns matching leads with their id — use that id for messaging_send.  Arguments:  query (required) — free-text search.limit (optional, default 20, max 100) — max results.

searchDocs.title: messaging_send​
searchDocs.content: Send a single one-off message to a specific lead. For multi-step sequenced outreach to many leads, build a campaign with campaigns_create + add_campaign_steps instead.  Arguments:  leadId (required) — Sonity lead id (from leads_search).text (required) — body text of the message.

searchDocs.title: The {variable} fallback rule​
searchDocs.content: When you create or update campaign steps with campaigns_create or add_campaign_steps, any step whose text contains personalization variables like {name}, {company}, or {title} must also supply a fallback_text. If it doesn't, the call throws:  Step 0 ("Connection Message") references variables {name}, {company} but has no fallback_text. Either provide a fallback_text on the step, or pass auto_fallback: true to use generic replacements (e.g. {name}→"there", {company}→"your company").   This protects you from sending literally {name} to a lead whose first name is missing.

searchDocs.title: Two ways to satisfy the rule​
searchDocs.content: Supply fallback_text per step — a safe generic version of the message. Recommended for high-stakes first-touch steps.Pass auto_fallback: true — the server replaces each variable with a generic placeholder: {name}, {first_name}, {full_name} → there{company}, {company_name}, {employer} → your company{title}, {job_title}, {position}, {role} → your role{industry}, {sector} → your industry{location}, {city}, {country}, {region} → your area / your country / your region{school}, {university}, {college} → your schoolany unknown variable → there  See also Personalization variables and merge tags for the broader variables story in Sonity.

searchDocs.title: Where to next​
searchDocs.content: Troubleshooting — common tool-call errors.Connecting a client — if you haven't wired up a client yet.

searchDocs.title: "Authorization header is required in MCP server config"​
searchDocs.content: You connected a client but didn't paste the Authorization header into it.  Fix  Open the in-app MCP dialog (sidebar → Bot icon → MCP connection), click Authorize MCP, approve the scopes, then copy the displayed Authorization: Bearer ... value into your client's config under headers.Authorization. See Connecting a client.

searchDocs.title: "Invalid MCP token" / "Invalid Sonity access token: ..."​
searchDocs.content: The token is wrong, expired, or doesn't match what the server expects.  Common causes  Token expired. Access tokens live 1 hour. Re-authorize via the in-app dialog.Token got cut off. The Bearer prefix is required, followed by the full token. Make sure nothing trimmed the end of it or broke it across multiple lines.You copied an old token from somewhere else. Always use the value shown in the current MCP dialog.  Fix  Open the MCP dialog, click Authorize MCP again, and copy the fresh token into your client's config.

searchDocs.title: "Missing required scope(s): mcp:write"​
searchDocs.content: Your token only allows reading, but you tried to do something that writes data (like creating a campaign, updating one, or sending a message).  Fix  Re-authorize via the in-app dialog. The dialog asks for mcp:read mcp:write profile sonity_account_id by default — make sure you didn't uncheck mcp:write on the consent page. If you approved a read-only token before, click Remove MCP authorization first, then Authorize MCP again to start fresh.

searchDocs.title: "Step N ('...') references variables like {name} or {company} but has no fallback_text"​
searchDocs.content: You created a campaign step that uses personalization placeholders like \{name\} or \{company\} (so the message says "Hi \{name\}, ...") but didn't tell the server what to put in if we don't know the lead's name.  Fix  Pick one of these:  Add a fallback_text to the step — a safe generic version of the message that's used when we don't have the lead's info, orPass auto_fallback: true when you create the step, and the server will fill in generic replacements automatically (for example \{name\} becomes "there", \{company\} becomes "your company", and so on).  See The \{variable\} fallback rule for the full list of replacements.

searchDocs.title: "405 Method not allowed" on GET /mcp or DELETE /mcp​
searchDocs.content: This is expected behavior, not an error. The MCP server only accepts POST /mcp requests. Anything else gets a 405 Method not allowed response.  Fix  Nothing to fix on your end. If your AI client is sending GET or DELETE, it's not using the MCP HTTP transport correctly — switch it to POST.

searchDocs.title: "sonity_account_id claim missing or invalid"​
searchDocs.content: Your token doesn't say which Sonity account you want to act on, so the server doesn't know what to do.  Fix  Re-authorize via the in-app dialog and make sure sonity_account_id is in the requested scopes (it is by default).

searchDocs.title: Still stuck​
searchDocs.content: Re-read Authentication to make sure your token is valid and not expired.Re-read Connecting a client to double-check your client config syntax.Open the Sonity UI's MCP dialog and click Remove MCP authorization, then Authorize MCP again for a clean slate.Contact support if the problem keeps happening.

searchDocs.title: Common variables​
searchDocs.content: {firstname}{lastname}{company}{position}  Variables are replaced with contact data at send time.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template:  Hi {firstname}, I saw your work at {company}.  Rendered output:  Hi Grace, I saw your work at Acme Labs.

searchDocs.title: Best practices​
searchDocs.content: Keep fallback messages for missing data cases.Do not overuse variables in one message.Preview templates before launching campaigns.Keep tone natural and concise.

searchDocs.title: 1. Sonity Profile​
searchDocs.content: The key is used to generate campaign steps and any other general content that we will introduce in the future  To add your API key for a given profile:  Go to the profile page.    Click the key icon to open the API key settings dialog.Click New KeySelect platformSkip endpoint for nowSelect the type of model you want to use  tip To conserve token usage, avoid selecting higher tier models. You should be able to generate meaningful steps with lower to medium tier models  7. Click Save

searchDocs.title: 2. Schedule Posts​
searchDocs.content: This key is used to generate posts for your campaign only. At the time of writing, its not used for anything else.  To use AI to generate posts for your campaign, take the following steps:  Open a campaign of the type Schedule PostsClick the Settings tab and scroll down to AI Personalization settingsFill in the settings  Profession — what role the AI should write as (e.g. blogger, journalist, marketer)Content Tone — the mood or feel of the writing (e.g. formal, casual, playful)Writing Style — the structural approach to the writing (e.g. narrative, analytical, conversational)Topics & Interests — the subjects the AI should focus on (e.g. technology, AI, finance)AI Model — the model used to generate posts (e.g. Claude Sonnet, GPT-4)API Key — your personal API key for authenticating with the chosen model    Click Save AI Personalization button  info In the future we may end specifying them as global keys and local keys. Global keys will be used to generate any kind of profile and local keys will be used to generate content specific to the campaign.  caution Make sure your personalization settings are not too loose or strict. Loose settings may result in AI writing content that is not relevant to your campaign, while strict settings my prevent the AI from being flexible. Think of an actor that has range vs an actor that does not have a range — the former can write about a wide variety of topics, while the latter may only write about a narrow range of topics. Garbage In, Garbage Out

searchDocs.title: Generating Steps
searchDocs.content: Generating Steps To generate steps using AI, follow these steps: On the campaign page go to the Steps Tab 2. Under a specific step, click generate tip You can specify the direction AI you want to take by mentioning the context in the entry box. This will help the AI generate a more relevant step instead of a generic one. Wait for the AI to generate the step

searchDocs.title: Wrong API Key​
searchDocs.content: If you are using an incorrect API key, you may encounter the following error:    To resolve this error, make sure you are using the correct API key.

searchDocs.title: Quota Exceeded​
searchDocs.content: If you have exceeded your quota, you may encounter the following error:  AI generation failed because your API key quota is exceeded. Please check your OpenAI plan and billing details.   To resolve this error, make sure you have not exceeded your quota. You can check your quota usage in your account dashboard.

searchDocs.title: Can I use proxies with Sonity?
searchDocs.content: Can I use proxies with Sonity? Yes, you can. Proxies in Sonity are managed on a profile basis. You can change and set proxies from the Profile settings to enhance your privacy and security. For more info on this please Read this guide

searchDocs.title: Why are my requests not sending?​
searchDocs.content: Check:  Profile execution window.Daily limit settings.Whether contacts are queued in the current step.

searchDocs.title: My campaign is paused. Why?​
searchDocs.content: Common reasons:  Daily activity limit reached.Profile/session issue.Configuration issue in steps.  See also: Common errors and what they mean.

searchDocs.title: How do I disconnect a LinkedIn profile?​
searchDocs.content: Open the profile settings in Sonity and remove or disconnect the profile from the workspace. Confirm that no active campaigns are bound to it before disconnecting.

searchDocs.title: Can I keep my browser closed while campaigns run?​
searchDocs.content: Yes. Sonity runs server-side and does not require your browser to stay open.

searchDocs.title: How do I safely increase campaign volume?​
searchDocs.content: Increase slowly over time, monitor acceptance and reply rates, and reduce limits immediately if performance drops.

searchDocs.title: How to read and act on analytics
Key metrics to monitor​
searchDocs.pageTitle: How to read and act on analytics
searchDocs.content: Connection acceptance rate.Reply rate.Step completion rate.Error or fallback usage rate.

searchDocs.title: How to act on low performance​
searchDocs.pageTitle: How to read and act on analytics
searchDocs.content: Low acceptance rate: Improve targeting and connection message quality.Low reply rate: Refine message relevance and CTA clarity.Low completion rate: Reduce delays that are too long or remove friction in the sequence.High fallback usage: Fix missing personalization fields in contacts.

searchDocs.title: Review cadence​
searchDocs.pageTitle: How to read and act on analytics
searchDocs.content: Check campaign performance daily during the first week, then move to a weekly optimization cycle.  For event-level analysis, review Campaign metrics.

searchDocs.title: How Sonity handles limits​
searchDocs.content: Sonity monitors account activity and pacing.Sonity applies throttling when risk signals appear.Sonity can delay, pause, or reduce actions automatically.Sonity cannot force actions when LinkedIn has already blocked them.

searchDocs.title: What you may see when limits are exceeded​
searchDocs.content: Temporary slowdown in campaign execution.Delayed or paused actions.

searchDocs.title: Recommended operating ranges​
searchDocs.content: Connection requests: usually 80-100/day on healthy paid accounts.Free accounts: significantly lower safe ranges, especially with notes.Profile retrieval: around 100/day per account is a common safe baseline.Search retrieval: split broad searches into smaller filtered segments.InMail: keep activity paced and randomized.

searchDocs.title: Final note​
searchDocs.content: As Sonity, we manage automation limits for your account. If thresholds are exceeded, we can throttle account activity to protect account health and reduce LinkedIn restrictions.

The Sonity tools will appear under the tools menu.

searchDocs.title: Cursor​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: Edit ~/.cursor/mcp.json:  { "mcpServers": { "sonity": { "url": "https://app.sonity.net/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer PASTE_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" } } } }   Restart Cursor. In the chat panel, switch the model selector to an agent mode that supports MCP.

searchDocs.title: Zed​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: Edit ~/.config/zed/settings.json and add the Sonity server under extension.context_servers:  { "extension": { "context_servers": { "sonity": { "command": { "transport": { "kind": "http", "url": "https://app.sonity.net/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer PASTE_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" } } } } } } }   Restart Zed. The Sonity tools will be available in the Assistant panel.

searchDocs.title: Cline​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: Edit cline_mcp_settings.json (use the Cline extension's "MCP Servers" → "Edit JSON" command):  { "mcpServers": { "sonity": { "url": "https://app.sonity.net/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer PASTE_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" }, "disabled": false, "alwaysAllow": [] } } }   Reload the Cline panel. The Sonity server should show as connected.

searchDocs.title: Raw cURL / scripting​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: The MCP HTTP transport speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST /mcp. A minimal session is two requests: initialize, then one or more tools/call.

searchDocs.title: 1. Initialize the session​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: curl -X POST https://app.sonity.net/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer PASTE_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize", "params": { "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": { "name": "curl", "version": "1.0" } } }'

searchDocs.title: 2. Call a tool — list your profiles​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: curl -X POST https://app.sonity.net/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer PASTE_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "profiles", "arguments": {} } }'   The response is a JSON-RPC result whose result.content[0].text is a JSON string with the profiles. Grab the id of the profile you want to act as — that's your sonity_profile_id for every other tool.  tip For anything beyond a quick test, use the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk instead of raw cURL. It handles session lifecycle, retries, and SSE streaming for you.

searchDocs.title: Verify it works​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Connecting an MCP client to Sonity
searchDocs.content: Whichever client you chose, the simplest smoke test is to ask the AI:  "List my Sonity profiles."  The AI should call the profiles tool and return a list with at least one profile. If you see an error, jump to Troubleshooting.
